TestPort_IsolationAbortedKeyrevoke PASS (strict) — all permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3. A SAVEPOINT-issued key UPDATE (KEY REVOKE) rolled back via ROLLBACK TO must not leave a phantom conflicting lock; s2 FOR KEY SHARE stays compatible. M0118-0009 design 0118-0014: SAVEPOINT eagerly materialises the top-level XID before AllocateSubXid so the subxid->parent link is non-zero from birth (parent=0 previously made the subxact writes cross-session-visible and defeated the row-lock wait); sub-XID-scoped NEW-tuple xmin + HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED on the single-xid old-tuple xmax stamp; descendant-direction subxact self-visibility in isCurrentTxXID.

Passes — TestPort_IsolationClassroomScheduling (internal/testport/isolation_port_test.go) matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte across all generated permutations; verified stable 3/3 runs. A SERIALIZABLE double-booking write-skew — s1 reads room_reservation with an overlap predicate then INSERTs an overlapping booking; s2 reads with its own overlap predicate then UPDATEs the existing booking's start_time into the contested window — where any overlap must raise 40001. Zero-SSI-change promotion: the dangerous-structure detection already validated on the prior 24 specs produces the exact abort pattern because the inserted/updated rows fall within the concurrent readers' overlap predicates so the relation/tuple-grain SIREAD locks cross-cover identically to PG. Two global-setup blockers had to clear. First — btree key-type support: the PRIMARY KEY (room_id text; start_time timestamptz) rejected the timestamptz key (0A000 btree v0 only supports int4 / numeric keys) at global setup. Fix: timestamptz is now an accepted btree key type that reuses the int64-micros-since-epoch timestamp key path (EncodeTimestamp) since timestamp and timestamptz share the same on-disk form — encodeBTreeKeyForColumn plus both index-only key decoders — so probe and backfill keys are byte-identical. Second — seconds-less timestamptz literal parse: the spec books rooms on the half-hour with literals like TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE '2010-04-01 10:00' (no seconds) which evalTypedStringLit rejected with 22007 until its timestamp/timestamptz layout list also accepted HH:MM and numeric-offset forms — verified by TestEvalTypedStringLitTimestampForms and a deterministic 5/5 TestPort_IsolationClassroomScheduling (previously 0/8 SKIP masked by a stale Go test cache).

TestPort_IsolationDeadlockHard PASS — eight sessions each LOCK TABLE their own relation then attempt to LOCK the next in a ring (s1→a2 … s8→a1) forming an 8-way cycle. Each session sets deadlock_timeout=100s except s8 (10ms) so s8 waits the shortest and runs the detector first; the general timeout-driven wait-for-graph detector finds the multi-relation cycle and rolls back the discovering session s8 with 40P01. New engine work: deadlock_timeout is now a registered superuser-set GUC (config.defaults) plumbed per-session into lockmgr via the new AcquireWithTimeout used by executor.acquireRelLockTxn (Context.deadlockTimeout reads the effective GUC); the timer-driven check (runDeadlockCheckFor / checkDeadlockLockedFor) prefers the firing backend as victim when it is in the cycle mirroring PostgreSQL DeadLockCheck — CheckDeadlocksNow keeps youngest-in-cycle selection. The isolation runner now honours the (*) BlockerStar permutation marker (hasStarBlocker) rendering the annotated step in waiting/completed format even when goopg observed it complete immediately so s8a1(*) shows the <waiting ...> marker the spec expects. M0118-0004.

Became an in-scope porting target after goopg implemented the REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE isolation levels (M0104); previously out of scope while only READ COMMITTED was supported — targeted for pass-through by M0118.

TestPort_IsolationDeadlockSimple PASS — two sessions each take ACCESS SHARE on a1 then each attempts a lock upgrade to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; the second upgrader closes a simple lock-upgrade deadlock cycle which PostgreSQL resolves synchronously (JoinWaitQueue early_deadlock) without waiting for deadlock_timeout so the victim errors immediately with no <waiting> marker. New engine work: lockmgr.Acquire now runs lockState.hasSimpleDeadlock before parking — when the requester already holds a lock here and would queue behind a conflicting waiter that itself conflicts with the requester's held locks the requester is the victim and gets lockmgr.ErrDeadlockDetected (mapped to SQLSTATE 40P01) immediately after releasing its other holdings (mirroring the timeout victim path) so the surviving upgrader proceeds. M0118-0003.

TestPort_IsolationDeadlockSoft2 PASS — s1 (deadlock_timeout 10ms) blocks for SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on a2 behind two ACCESS EXCLUSIVE waiters s3 and s4 that are themselves hard-blocked on s2's ACCESS SHARE holder. s1's request does not conflict with the holder so the soft-deadlock resolver topologically reorders a2's multi-waiter queue (s1 ahead of s3 and s4) via topoSort and grants s1 immediately rather than aborting anyone. Shares the soft-edge engine added for deadlock-soft (checkDeadlockLockedFor → findLockCycle → deadLockCheck/testConfiguration → expandConstraints/topoSort → applyWaitOrders). M0118-0004.

TestPort_IsolationDeadlockSoft PASS — four sessions form a 4-cycle with two hard edges (e1→d1 e2→d2: an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE waiter behind an ACCESS SHARE holder) and two soft edges (d2→e1 d1→e2: an ACCESS SHARE waiter queued behind a conflicting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE waiter). Because the cycle contains soft edges the detector resolves it by reordering a2's wait queue (moving d1 ahead of e2) so d1 is granted immediately and nobody is rolled back. New engine work: lockmgr.checkDeadlockLockedFor now runs a soft-aware search on the timer path mirroring deadlock.c — findLockCycle records soft (queue-order) edges; deadLockCheck/testConfiguration try reversing them; expandConstraints/topoSort rebuild the affected wait queues; applyWaitOrders rewrites the queue and wakes newly grantable waiters. CheckDeadlocksNow keeps the legacy hard-only youngest-victim path. M0118-0004.

TestPort_IsolationDeleteAbortSavept2 PASS (strict) — all permutations byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3. A SELF lock-only upgrade inside a SAVEPOINT (FOR KEY SHARE -> FOR NO KEY UPDATE under the sub-XID) rolled back via ROLLBACK TO must revert to the outer FOR KEY SHARE strength; a conflicting FOR UPDATE waiter keeps waiting on the restored lock. M0118-0009 design 0118-0015: the savepoint upgrade routes through stampMultiLock (gate widened by hasOuterSelfLockMember) so the outer top-level KEY SHARE survives as a multi member; ROLLBACK TO drops only the sub-XID member.

TestPort_IsolationDeleteAbortSavept PASS — all 7 permutations. A DELETE inside a SAVEPOINT over a row the same xact already locked FOR KEY SHARE is a lock upgrade; ROLLBACK TO must restore the outer KEY SHARE lock. Three engine fixes (M0118-0009 design 0118-0013): heap DELETE/UPDATE now stamp the old tuple xmax (and its WAL record) under the effective writer xid (current sub-XID inside a savepoint) via effectiveWriterXID rather than the top-level XID so an aborted-subxact deletion is identifiable; the multixact producer preserves an outer-level self locker into {outer-keyshare + subxid-updater} so dropping the rolled-back subxid member leaves the KEY SHARE alive; lockRowsOp stampLockInner treats a subxact-aborted xmax (IsAborted) as a rolled-back updater (row live at original ptr) not a committed delete. s2 FOR UPDATE waits on the restored outer lock then proceeds after s1 commits.

TestPort_IsolationMultixactNoDeadlock PASS — s1 takes FOR SHARE on the single row then s2 also takes FOR SHARE turning the tuple lock into a multixact; s3 then requests FOR UPDATE which conflicts with the SHARE multixact and waits. TestPort_IsolationMultixactNoForget PASS — all 9 permutations. s1 holds FOR KEY SHARE then s2 UPDATEs (forming a {s1-keyshare + s2-no-key-update} multixact); when s2 aborts the surviving s1 lock must not be forgotten and when s2 commits the lock must be carried forward onto the new tuple version. Fix 1 — the keyConflict branch of lockRowsOp.stampLockInner now builds its multi-member wait set from conflictingLockHolders rather than activeLockHolders so a non-conflicting surviving locker is not waited on (s3 FOR NO KEY UPDATE no longer blocks on s1 FOR KEY SHARE after s2 aborts; only s3 FOR UPDATE still conflicts and waits); and stampAtPtr now preserves surviving lockers via stampMultiLock so the aborted-updater stamp keeps s1's lock alive. Fix 2 — the HOT UPDATE producer carries the old tuple's non-conflicting lockers forward onto the new tuple version (carryForwardLockersToNewTuple — the new-version half of heap_update compute_new_xmax_infomask — sharing survivingLockersForUpdate with the old-tuple stamp) so after s2 commits s3 FOR UPDATE waits on the inherited FOR KEY SHARE until s1 commits.

Promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict TestPort_IsolationPredicateHash (design 0118-0099). PAGE (bucket) level predicate locking in a hash index. A declared-hash index (catalog.Index.DeclaredHash — Method stays btree on goopg's B-tree substrate) now drives a bucket-grain SIREAD predicate lock keyed by the index OID + a stable hash of the encoded equality key (ssiRecordHashBucketRead on the index scan / index-only scan; ssiRecordHashIndexInsert on the INSERT path) in place of a seq scan's relation-grain lock. The per-tuple heap reads switch to conflict-out-only (ssiConflictOutTupleRead) so they do not coarsen to a heap-page lock that would re-introduce a different-bucket false positive. Result: same-bucket scan/insert interleavings still conflict (40001) while the 12 different-bucket interleavings goopg previously over-aborted now commit — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 40 permutations. Blast radius bounded to SERIALIZABLE equality scans on declared-hash indexes; the pass-required btree/seqscan SSI specs are unaffected.

Passes — TestPort_IsolationReadOnlyAnomaly3 (internal/testport/isolation_port_test.go) matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte. Two blockers were fixed: the DEFERRABLE keyword token was never consumed by parseBeginModes (acceptIdentKeyword vs acceptKeyword) and the safe-snapshot drain-the-writers deferral did not exist. Passes — TestPort_IsolationTemporalRangeIntegrity (internal/testport/isolation_port_test.go) matches PG 18.3 byte-for-byte across all generated permutations; verified stable 3/3 runs at ~2.5s each. A SERIALIZABLE temporal write-skew across two tables — s1 reads statute with a date-range predicate then INSERTs offense; s2 reads offense with a date-range predicate then DELETEs statute — where any overlap must raise 40001. Zero-SSI-change promotion: the dangerous-structure detection already validated on the prior 23 specs produces the exact abort pattern because the deleted statute row and the inserted offense row both fall within the concurrent readers' predicates so the relation/tuple-grain SIREAD locks cross-cover identically to PG — including the empty-relation predicate reads. The sole blocker was btree key-type support: the statute PRIMARY KEY (statute_cite text; eff_date date) rejected the date key (0A000 btree v0 only supports int4 / numeric keys; got date) at global setup. Fix: date is now an accepted btree key type encoded order-preservingly via the int4-days-since-epoch path (encodeBTreeKeyForColumn plus both index-only key decoders) mirroring the codec date encoding so probe and backfill keys are byte-identical.

Passes — row-level half via TestPort_TimeoutsRowLevel and table-level half via TestPort_TimeoutsTableLevel (internal/testport/timeouts_rowlock_test.go); both 4/4 matching PG 18.3 cancel messages and ~300ms timing. TestPort_IsolationTuplelockPartition PASS — INSERT ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE on a LIST-partitioned table. A no-key UPDATE arm (SET col1/col2) does not conflict with a concurrent FOR KEY SHARE so s2 proceeds; a key UPDATE arm (SET key=1) blocks s2 until s1 commits even though the key value is unchanged. Two fixes in the upsert applyUpdate path: (1) onConflictUpdateTouchesKeyColumn stamps HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED on the conflicting tuple whenever the DO UPDATE SET list assigns a unique/primary-key column — mirroring PG ExecUpdateLockMode which keys off the updated-column set (ExecGetAllUpdatedCols) not value comparison so a FOR KEY SHARE waits; (2) stampOldCtid now links the old tuple to the new version so a waiting FOR KEY SHARE follows the ctid chain to the live successor instead of short-reading a self-pointing ctid. TestPort_IsolationTuplelockUpdate PASS — s1 builds an update chain via UPDATE pktab SET data = DEFAULT then takes FOR KEY SHARE on the live row while s2/s3/s4 each hold a pending no-key UPDATE gated behind one of three advisory locks s1 owns. Releasing each advisory lock in turn lets that updater follow the ctid chain and propagate the KEY SHARE lock forward onto the new version without conflicting (no-key update does not conflict with KEY SHARE). Two fixes landed: (1) planner defaultMarkerReplacement rewrites an explicit DEFAULT keyword on a SERIAL or identity column to nextval('<table>_<col>_seq') instead of NULL because goopg leaves the catalog DefaultExpr nil for serial columns so the bare DEFAULT previously collapsed to NULL and tripped the SERIAL NOT NULL constraint; (2) the isolation runner now honours BlockerStepComplete annotations such as s1_advunlock1(s2_update) by rendering the unlock step in waiting/completed format with its report gated behind the referenced pending blocker step. M0118-0003.

TestPort_IsolationTuplelockUpgradeNoDeadlock PASS — all 9 permutations. Perm 9 exercises savepoint-scoped row-lock upgrades: s1 takes FOR KEY SHARE then upgrades to FOR SHARE inside savepoint e and FOR NO KEY UPDATE inside savepoint f while s2 waits to upgrade its own FOR KEY SHARE to FOR NO KEY UPDATE; ROLLBACK TO s1_e must revert the FOR SHARE upgrade so s2 becomes grantable exactly there (not at the full ROLLBACK). New engine work: lockRowsOp now stamps each lock member under the effective writer xid (the current sub-XID via session.EffectiveWriterXID) instead of the top-level xid (the writerXID helper) and every row-lock self check resolves the whole transaction tree to its top-level ancestor (the isSelfXID helper via Manager.TopLevelXid) so a subtransaction never blocks on or clobbers its own parent or sibling member; stampMultiLock keeps outer-level self members as survivors and re-adds only the current sub-XID member. Manager.AllocateSubXid now registers the sub-XID through RegisterSubXid so the attached pg_subtrans SubxactMap (the real-server path) resolves TopLevelXid and IsAborted — otherwise xidActiveWithSubxact reported the savepoint lock dead and conflicting waiters never blocked. M0118-0004 (docs/design/0118-0012).
